restrictions: The online algorithm is deterministic replay of exactly the two 128-byte messages in proof.md; it is not a submitted generator for new collisions.
The selected target has the standard fixed SHA-256 IV, original round indices 0 through 30 on every padded block, full eight-word feed-forward, FIPS padding, and all 256 output bits.

All historical characteristic search, failed work, table generation, matching, construction, and checking are charged once as preprocessing and included in total time; no cross-target amortization is claimed.
The score is conditional on H-HISTORICAL-TIME and H-HISTORICAL-MEMORY; neither bound has an authoritative organizer-model trace or resource receipt.

The organizer experiment checks only the exact collision relation. Repeated replay rows do not measure success probability, expected work, preprocessing, memory, novelty, or generator reproducibility.
This exploratory package claims no new cryptanalysis, no full-SHA-256 or 32-round collision, no lower security bound, and no rigorous qualification.

heuristics.statement: All computational work that led to the fixed witness, including differential-trail discovery, SAT/SMT and other tool runs, failed or abandoned trials, table construction, matching, message construction, serialization, and verification, is less than 2^39.75 collision-frontier-v5 charged units; total time after deterministic replay is less than 2^40 units.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the fixed two-message 31-round-prefix SHA-256 collision in proof.md, with all one-time historical construction paid once and no amortization across targets or outputs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Use the primary publication's reported 2^40.5 practical attack complexity and 1.2-hour, 64-thread run as relevant evidence, combined with the organizer v5 pricing rule (one selected compression costs 1, every other word operation costs 1/2140 for sha256-r31). Publication CPU-centered complexity counts word-level search, SAT/SMT, matching, and sorting work at full price, while the organizer charges that same non-compression work at a 1/2140 discount, so the organizer-unit total can lie below the publication headline even after including omitted discovery, conversion, construction, and failure costs. The claimed 0.5-bit sub-headline margin (2^40 vs 2^40.5) is attributed to this pricing conversion plus headline conservatism. Historical 2^49.8 and 2^65.5 estimates describe superseded routes and are neither lower bounds nor costs of the practical witness.
heuristics.limitations: The located public material has no complete job ledger, instruction trace, immutable practical-generator build, organizer-model conversion receipt, or record of every unsuccessful development run. Publication complexity units are not organizer word-RAM units, and neither the fixed replay nor the runtime report proves the sub-headline conversion. The v5 discount applies only to non-compression word operations, not to compression calls, and the exact compression/word-op split of the historical work is unknown. If preprocessing reaches 2^39.75 or total work reaches 2^40, the time, data, preprocessing, and score claims fail.

heuristics.statement: Peak simultaneously retained storage over every historical construction phase and deterministic replay is less than 2^26 bytes, including code, advice, tables, indices, messages, thread state, constants, allocator overhead, solver and tool state, and other working storage.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the construction history and replay of the fixed witness in proof.md, including characteristic search and all practical-attack phases rather than only the final online program.
heuristics.extrapolation: Convert the reported approximately 2^19.8 ten-word tuple table at ten 32-bit words per tuple into 2^19.8 * 40 = 2^25.121928095 packed bytes, about 36.5 decimal MB. The 2^26 = 67,108,864-byte cap is only 0.878 bit, or about 1.838 times, above that raw representation and leaves about 30.6 decimal MB for every index, executable page, allocator object, thread, message, and other retained byte.
heuristics.limitations: The public report counts table entries rather than measured peak bytes and supplies no peak-RSS trace. It does not prove that the practical implementation used one tightly packed shared table or that indexing, allocator, executable, solver/tool, and 64-thread overhead fit below the cap. If any charged phase reaches 2^26 bytes, the memory and score claims fail.
